anat-cns-overview.intro: Start with the big picture from three sides: the lobes from the side, the midline structures from the middle, and the underside where the cranial nerves come off. Explore each drawing, then switch to Quiz mode.

plates.title: Lobes & Functional Areas (Lateral)
plates.caption: Lateral view of the left hemisphere, anterior on the left: frontal lobe (red), parietal lobe (gray), temporal lobe (blue), occipital lobe (green), cerebellum and brainstem (tan). Source: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology (Wikimedia Commons, 1306 Lobes of Cerebral Cortex), CC BY 4.0; labels and leader lines removed.

hotspots.label: Frontal Lobe
hotspots.blurb: Executive function, personality, judgment. Frontal tumors present with personality change or seizures.

hotspots.label: Precentral Gyrus (Motor Cortex)
hotspots.blurb: Primary motor strip: contralateral weakness. Arranged as a homunculus (leg medial, face lateral).

hotspots.label: Broca's Area
hotspots.blurb: Inferior frontal gyrus, dominant hemisphere: expressive (non-fluent) aphasia.

hotspots.label: Postcentral Gyrus (Sensory Cortex)
hotspots.blurb: Primary somatosensory cortex: contralateral numbness.

hotspots.label: Parietal Lobe
hotspots.blurb: Sensory integration; non-dominant lesions cause neglect; dominant lesions cause Gerstmann syndrome.

hotspots.label: Wernicke's Area
hotspots.blurb: Posterior superior temporal gyrus, dominant hemisphere: receptive (fluent) aphasia.

hotspots.label: Temporal Lobe
hotspots.blurb: Hearing, language, memory (medial temporal/hippocampus). Temporal tumors cause seizures, often with auras.

hotspots.label: Occipital Lobe
hotspots.blurb: Visual cortex: contralateral homonymous hemianopia.

hotspots.label: Sylvian (Lateral) Fissure
hotspots.blurb: Separates the frontal/parietal lobes from the temporal lobe. The MCA runs in it.

hotspots.label: Cerebellum
hotspots.blurb: Coordination: ipsilateral ataxia and dysmetria.

hotspots.label: Brainstem
hotspots.blurb: Cranial nerve nuclei and long tracts. A key organ at risk: injury causes major neurologic deficits.

plates.title: Midline Structures (Sagittal)
plates.caption: The brain cut down the middle, anterior on the left: corpus callosum, thalamus, hypothalamus, pituitary, the three parts of the brainstem, and the cerebellum. Patrick J. Lynch, medical illustrator (Wikimedia Commons), CC BY 2.5.

hotspots.label: Corpus Callosum
hotspots.blurb: The thick bundle of white matter that connects the two hemispheres. Tumor crossing it to the other side ('butterfly' pattern) suggests glioblastoma or lymphoma.

hotspots.label: Cingulate Gyrus
hotspots.blurb: The gyrus wrapped around the corpus callosum. Part of the limbic system: emotion, motivation, and attention.

hotspots.label: Fornix
hotspots.blurb: An arched tract that carries output from the hippocampus forward to the hypothalamus. Part of the memory circuit.

hotspots.label: Thalamus
hotspots.blurb: The relay station: almost every sensory signal (except smell) passes through it on the way to the cortex. Deep tumors here are usually biopsied, not resected.

hotspots.label: Hypothalamus
hotspots.blurb: Sits below the thalamus and controls the pituitary, temperature, thirst, and appetite. Dose here can cause hormone deficits.

hotspots.label: Pituitary Gland
hotspots.blurb: Hangs from the hypothalamus by the stalk and sits in the sella turcica, just below the optic chiasm. Its tumors press up on the chiasm.

hotspots.label: Midbrain
hotspots.blurb: Top of the brainstem. Holds the nuclei for CN III and IV (eye movements) and the cerebral aqueduct.

hotspots.label: Pons
hotspots.blurb: The bulge in the middle of the brainstem. Holds the nuclei for CN V to VIII and relays signals to the cerebellum. A key organ at risk.

hotspots.label: Medulla
hotspots.blurb: Bottom of the brainstem. Controls breathing, heart rate, and swallowing (CN IX to XII). Continues into the spinal cord at the foramen magnum.

hotspots.label: Spinal Cord
hotspots.blurb: Leaves the skull through the foramen magnum and runs down to about L1 to L2.

hotspots.label: Fourth Ventricle
hotspots.blurb: The CSF space between the brainstem and the cerebellum. A posterior fossa tumor that blocks it causes hydrocephalus.

hotspots.label: Cerebellum
hotspots.blurb: Coordination and balance. A lesion causes ataxia on the same side of the body.

hotspots.label: Occipital Lobe
hotspots.blurb: Vision. The calcarine sulcus on this medial surface is the primary visual cortex.

plates.title: The Underside: Cranial Nerves
plates.caption: The brain from below, anterior at the top, with the cranial nerves cut where they leave the brain. Patrick J. Lynch, medical illustrator (Wikimedia Commons), CC BY 2.5.

hotspots.label: Olfactory Tract (CN I)
hotspots.blurb: Smell. Runs along the floor of the frontal lobe. Olfactory groove meningiomas sit here.

hotspots.label: Optic Nerve (CN II)
hotspots.blurb: Vision. Runs back from each eye through the optic canal. An organ at risk: injury means blindness.

hotspots.label: Optic Chiasm
hotspots.blurb: Where the nasal fibers from each eye cross. Sits right above the pituitary, so a pituitary tumor causes bitemporal hemianopia.

hotspots.label: Pituitary Stalk
hotspots.blurb: Connects the hypothalamus to the pituitary gland in the sella (cut here).

hotspots.label: Oculomotor Nerve (CN III)
hotspots.blurb: Moves most of the eye muscles and the eyelid; constricts the pupil. Runs through the cavernous sinus.

hotspots.label: Trochlear Nerve (CN IV)
hotspots.blurb: Superior oblique muscle (looking down and in). Thinnest cranial nerve; also passes through the cavernous sinus.

hotspots.label: Trigeminal Nerve (CN V)
hotspots.blurb: Facial sensation and chewing. Its V1 and V2 branches run in the cavernous sinus; trigeminal neuralgia can be treated with SRS.

hotspots.label: Abducens Nerve (CN VI)
hotspots.blurb: Lateral rectus (looking out). Palsy causes horizontal double vision.

hotspots.label: Facial & Vestibulocochlear Nerves (CN VII, VIII)
hotspots.blurb: Leave the brainstem together at the cerebellopontine angle and enter the internal auditory canal. Vestibular schwannomas grow here.

hotspots.label: Lower Cranial Nerves (CN IX to XII)
hotspots.blurb: Swallowing, voice, and tongue movement. Exit near the jugular foramen and hypoglossal canal.

hotspots.label: Pons
hotspots.blurb: The bulge of the brainstem seen from below.

hotspots.label: Medulla
hotspots.blurb: Continues into the spinal cord.

hotspots.label: Cerebellum
hotspots.blurb: Fills the posterior fossa under the occipital lobes.

hotspots.label: Temporal Lobe
hotspots.blurb: Its inner (medial) surface holds the hippocampus. It sits right next to the cavernous sinus and the pituitary.

gallery.title: Homunculus
gallery.caption: Sensory homunculus on the postcentral gyrus; the motor strip just in front follows the same map: leg medial, arm and face lateral. Source: OpenStax College (Wikimedia Commons, 1421 Sensory Homunculus), CC BY 3.0.

anat-cns-deep.intro: Now look inside and around the brain: the deep gray matter on a coronal cut, the ventricles that carry CSF, and the tentorium that splits the skull into two compartments.

plates.title: Deep Structures (Coronal)
plates.caption: Coronal cut through the thalami, viewed from the front. Gray matter is the darker tan; white matter is the paler tan. Patrick J. Lynch, medical illustrator (Wikimedia Commons), CC BY 2.5.

hotspots.label: Cerebral Cortex (Gray Matter)
hotspots.blurb: The outer layer of nerve cell bodies, folded into gyri and sulci. This is where thinking, movement, and sensation are processed.

hotspots.label: White Matter
hotspots.blurb: Myelinated axons connecting regions of the cortex. Often the site of radiation leukoencephalopathy after whole-brain RT.

hotspots.label: Longitudinal Fissure
hotspots.blurb: Separates the two hemispheres. The falx cerebri dips down into it; parasagittal meningiomas grow along it.

hotspots.label: Corpus Callosum
hotspots.blurb: The white matter bridge between the hemispheres, forming the roof of the lateral ventricles.

hotspots.label: Lateral Ventricle
hotspots.blurb: Paired CSF spaces in each hemisphere. The choroid plexus here makes most of the CSF.

hotspots.label: Thalamus
hotspots.blurb: Deep gray matter on either side of the third ventricle. The relay station for sensation.

hotspots.label: Third Ventricle
hotspots.blurb: The thin midline CSF space between the two thalami. It drains through the cerebral aqueduct to the fourth ventricle.

hotspots.label: Basal Ganglia (Putamen)
hotspots.blurb: Deep gray matter lateral to the internal capsule. Controls movement (it is what fails in Parkinson's disease).

hotspots.label: Insula
hotspots.blurb: Cortex hidden deep in the lateral (Sylvian) fissure. Gliomas here are hard to resect.

hotspots.label: Temporal Lobe
hotspots.blurb: Hearing, language comprehension (dominant side), and memory through the hippocampus on its inner surface.

hotspots.label: Brainstem
hotspots.blurb: Connects the brain to the spinal cord. Its dose limit is one of the most important constraints in brain RT.

hotspots.label: Cerebellum
hotspots.blurb: Below the tentorium, behind the brainstem: the infratentorial compartment.

plates.title: Ventricles & CSF Flow
plates.caption: Midsagittal diagram of CSF flow (arrows): made by the choroid plexus in the ventricles, CSF passes through the 3rd ventricle, aqueduct, and 4th ventricle into the subarachnoid space and is absorbed at the arachnoid granulations. Source: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology (Wikimedia Commons, 1317 CFS Circulation), CC BY 4.0; labels and leader lines removed.

hotspots.label: Lateral Ventricles
hotspots.blurb: Where CSF is mostly made (choroid plexus). Enlarged with hydrocephalus.

hotspots.label: Foramen of Monro
hotspots.blurb: Connects each lateral ventricle to the 3rd. Colloid cysts here cause sudden hydrocephalus.

hotspots.label: 3rd Ventricle
hotspots.blurb: Midline, between the thalami.

hotspots.label: Cerebral Aqueduct (of Sylvius)
hotspots.blurb: Narrow channel through the midbrain; aqueductal stenosis or pineal tumors cause obstructive hydrocephalus.

hotspots.label: 4th Ventricle
hotspots.blurb: Drains via the foramina of Luschka (lateral) and Magendie (midline).

hotspots.label: Subarachnoid Space
hotspots.blurb: CSF bathes the brain and spinal cord. Leptomeningeal disease spreads here; medulloblastoma needs craniospinal RT.

plates.title: Compartments: Above and Below the Tentorium
plates.caption: Coronal schematic of the coverings: dura (yellow), CSF (blue), cerebrum (pink), and cerebellum (purple). Cancer Research UK diagram 386 (Wikimedia Commons), CC BY-SA 4.0; labels removed.

hotspots.label: Cerebrum (Supratentorial)
hotspots.blurb: Everything above the tentorium: the two hemispheres. Most adult brain tumors (gliomas, metastases, meningiomas) are supratentorial.

hotspots.label: Cerebellum (Infratentorial)
hotspots.blurb: Below the tentorium in the posterior fossa, with the brainstem. Most childhood brain tumors (medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma, ependymoma) are here.

hotspots.label: Tentorium Cerebelli
hotspots.blurb: A tent of dura between the cerebrum and cerebellum. It divides the skull into two compartments that behave very differently.

hotspots.label: Falx Cerebri
hotspots.blurb: A sheet of dura in the midline separating the two hemispheres.

hotspots.label: Dura Mater
hotspots.blurb: The tough outer covering of the brain (yellow). Meningiomas grow from the coverings.

hotspots.label: CSF Spaces
hotspots.blurb: CSF (blue) fills the ventricles and surrounds the brain and cord. Tumors that spread through it need the whole space treated (craniospinal RT).

hotspots.label: Spinal Cord & Canal
hotspots.blurb: The CSF space continues down around the spinal cord to the bottom of the thecal sac at about S2.
